{"slices":[{"index":0,"name":"Overdue Loans To Notify","x0":105.25,"x1":249.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: Overdue Loans To Notify

Intent

The list of overdue loans whose borrowers have not yet been sent an overdue notice. The overdue notice gateway works through it, so each borrower with an overdue loan is emailed once, as soon as the loan is overdue. Each item carries everything the email needs, so the gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the Overdue Notice Gateway, a system reaction in the Send Overdue Notice slice. No person reads this list, and it has no screen.
  • What the gateway does with it: for each loan on the list, it hands one notice to the email provider and records Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice slice). How often it checks the list is that slice's concern.

Read Model / View

  • View: Overdue Loans To Notify built from events: "Tool Added", "Neighbor Registered", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Overdue Notice Sent", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Overdue Notice Gateway (Send Overdue Notice). Internal: no ui.
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a loan is overdue is worked out when the list is read, from dueDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so a loan is on the list from the first read after midnight following its due date.

The view keeps one row for every open loan that hasn't been sent a notice; the query returns only the overdue ones. LoanId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId Tool Checked Out.loanId.
toolId ToolId Tool Checked Out.toolId.
neighborId NeighborId Tool Checked Out.neighborId: the borrower.
dueDate Date Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for this loan.
toolName Text Derived: Tool Added.name for toolId, copied under this name.
borrowerName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for neighborId, copied under this name.
borrowerEmail Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.email for neighborId, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor, copied under this name. Always the current one.
overdue Bool Derived: yes when today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate (INV-OLN-1). Worked out when the list is read.

Bookkeeping. To fill toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail the moment a loan starts, the view keeps the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and the name of every tool, not only those on a row. This is never returned except on the rows the query returns.

When a row leaves the view. A loan's row is removed when Overdue Notice Sent, Tool Returned or Tool Lost is recorded for it (INV-OLN-8). Nothing puts it back.

Queries

  • List loans to notify. Takes nothing. Returns every row whose overdue is yes, with loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate, toolName, borrowerName and borrowerEmail. There is no paging. The order doesn't matter to the gateway, which sends one notice per loan.

Invariants / Business Rules

A loan is ready for its notice as soon as it joins the list. When the email goes out, with no quiet hours, is Send Overdue Notice's rule (INV-OVN-6, Send Overdue Notice).

  • INV-OLN-1: A loan is on the list from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while the tool is still out and no overdue notice has been sent for it.
    • Overdue is worked out by comparing the due date with today. No event marks a loan overdue; the loan joins the list because the date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-2: A loan's due date is the one set at checkout, moved by each extension.
    • A loan extended before it became overdue joins the list only once its new due date has passed.
  • INV-OLN-3: Once an overdue notice is sent for a loan, the loan leaves the list and never comes back.
    • One notice per loan. An overdue loan can't be extended (INV-EXT-5, Extend Loan), so it stays overdue until it ends, and no second notice goes out.
  • INV-OLN-4: When the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost, its loan leaves the list.
    • A loan that ends this way before its notice went out never gets a notice.
    • A closed account never has a loan on the list, because an account can't be closed while tools are on loan (INV-CLS-7, Close Account).
    • A loan whose tool is retired while it is out stays on the list and still gets its notice: the loan carries on until the tool is returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-OLN-6: Each loan on the list carries everything the notice needs: the borrower's name and email, the tool's name, and the due date.
    • The borrower's name comes from Neighbor Registered, and the email is the borrower's current one: Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The tool's name comes from Tool Added, and the due date from Tool Checked Out, moved by any Loan Extended. The gateway looks nothing up elsewhere.
  • INV-OLN-8: A loan leaves the list only when an overdue notice is sent for it, when the tool is returned, or when the tool is recorded lost.
    • A notice that later fails to deliver doesn't put the loan back on the list. The failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and no further attempt is made.
  • INV-OLN-9: Applying the same event twice leaves the list as if it had been applied once.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Loan not yet overdue (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: Ana (N1) borrowing the cordless drill (T1), due 12 October
    • When: the list is read at 23:59 on 12 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is not returned.
  • Loan becomes overdue (INV-OLN-1, INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org; Tool Added for T1, "Cordless drill"; and L1 is due 12 October, still out
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: L1 is returned, with toolName "Cordless drill", borrowerName "Ana Ruiz", borrowerEmail ana@example.org, and dueDate 12 October.
  • Extended before it became overdue (INV-OLN-2)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for L1 on 10 October, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: L1 is not returned when the list is read on 13 October, and is returned from 00:00 on 20 October if still out.
  • Overdue notice sent (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-8)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and is never returned again while the drill is out.
  • Returned before the notice (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1 before any notice is sent
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is on the list
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: L1 leaves the list, and no notice is sent for it.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-OLN-4)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October and still out, and Tool Retired was recorded for T1 on 11 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned, ready for its notice.
  • Borrower changes their email (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is on the list, carrying ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • Then: L1 stays on the list, now carrying ana@example.org, so the notice goes to the new address.
  • Email changed before the loan is overdue (INV-OLN-6)
    • Given: L1 is due 12 October, and N1's email was changed to ana@example.org on 10 October
    • When: the list is read at 00:00 on 13 October
    • Then: L1 is returned carrying ana@example.org.
  • Several borrowers (INV-OLN-1)
    • Given: L1 (Ana, due 12 October) and L2 (Ben, due 14 October) are both out
    • When: the list is read on 13 October
    • Then: only L1 is returned.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: L1 is on the list once
    • When: the same Tool Checked Out for L1 is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still on the list once.
  • Replayed sent notice (INV-OLN-3, INV-OLN-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, so L1 is off the list
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Sent is applied again
    • Then: L1 is still off the list.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-OLN-9). An event applied a second time leaves the list as it was after the first.
  • Events for a loan that has left the list: once a loan's row is removed, a later Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost for it (a replay) changes nothing. An Overdue Notice Failed doesn't reach this list at all.
  • The gateway reads a loan twice before Overdue Notice Sent lands: the list may return the same loan on two reads in a row. Sending one notice per loan is the Send Overdue Notice slice's rule, enforced when it records Overdue Notice Sent; this list raises no errors of its own.
  • Daylight-saving changes: the day boundary is midnight in the shed's local time zone, whatever its offset from UTC that day.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: read only by the Overdue Notice Gateway. No person or screen reads it.
  • PII & compliance: holds the name and current email of every registered neighbor, and hands them to the gateway only for borrowers with an overdue loan. It shows them on no screen.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above. A loan is ready as soon as it joins the list; how soon the email goes out after that is Send Overdue Notice's concern.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • These match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/extend-loan.md and slices/my-loans.md. Change Email, Send Overdue Notice, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Send Overdue Notice, whose gateway works from this list and records Overdue Notice Sent.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":1,"name":"Send Overdue Notice","x0":274.25,"x1":418.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: Send Overdue Notice

Intent

Tell a borrower by email that their loan is overdue, once per loan, so they return the tool. The shed records that the notice was handed to the email provider. That record shows the borrower was told, and stops a second notice.

Trigger & Actor

  • Trigger form: internally triggered. The Overdue Notice Gateway, a translation to the email provider outside the shed, watches the Overdue Loans To Notify list (slices/overdue-loans-to- notify.md). No person sends notices; only the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice.
  • When it reads: the list fills when midnight passes in the shed's local time, not when an event arrives, so the gateway reads it every 5 minutes, at any hour. A loan is therefore noticed within 5 minutes of becoming overdue (INV-OVN-6).
  • What the gateway does, for each loan on the list:
    1. It issues Send Overdue Notice for the loan, with the content from the loan's item: borrowerEmail, borrowerName, toolName and dueDate. If the command is refused, or is a repeat, nothing is sent for that loan.
    2. Each recorded Overdue Notice Sent is handed to the provider from the event itself, using the loan ID as the hand-off's key. The hand-off is driven by the recorded event, not by the list: if the hand-off call errors, or the process stops before the provider accepts, it is repeated with the same key (after a restart too) until the provider accepts it. This is an outbox, not a domain event.
  • The email: to the address recorded on the event, giving the borrower's name, the tool's name and the due date recorded on it, asking them to return the tool, and saying that an overdue loan blocks new checkouts and pickups (INV-OVN-3, INV-OVN-7).
  • The email port's contract, from the shed's house rules: the provider accepts a hand-off with a key, sends at most one email per key, makes its own delivery attempts (3 over about an hour), and sends one final failure report quoting the key, signed so the shed can trust it. The final failure is recorded by Record Overdue Notice Failure (slices/record-overdue-notice- failure.md).

Command / Input

Command: Send Overdue Notice

A LoanId is a UUID. "Today" is the calendar date in the shed's local time zone at the moment the command is handled.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes The overdue loan. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-OVN-10), still open (INV-OVN-5) and overdue today (INV-OVN-6).
sentTo Text yes The address to send to: the borrower's current email, from the list item's borrowerEmail.
borrowerName Text yes From the list item. Shown in the email.
toolName Text yes From the list item. Shown in the email.
dueDate Date yes From the list item. Must be the loan's current due date (INV-OVN-11). Shown in the email.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Overdue Notice Gateway, also in this slice, reading Overdue Loans To Notify.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Overdue Notice Sent → context Loans Read by: Overdue Loans To Notify (the loan leaves the list for good) and My Loans (shows the borrower that a notice was sent).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command. Also the key of the hand-off, which the provider's failure report quotes back.
sentTo Text yes From the command: the address the notice went to.
borrowerName Text yes From the command: the name the notice was addressed to.
toolName Text yes From the command: the tool named in the notice.
dueDate Date yes From the command: the due date the notice gave.
sentAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

The address, name, tool name and due date are facts of the notice: what was actually sent. They are recorded on the event so the hand-off can be repeated, even after a restart, without the list, and so they don't change if the neighbor's details change later. This is the one kind of event that carries copies of names.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. The gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify, specified in slices/overdue-loans-to-notify.md. Overdue Notice Sent removes the loan from that list and marks the loan on My Loans. Both are eventually consistent: the list may still show a loan for a moment after its notice is recorded, which is why the command itself refuses a second notice.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-OVN-2: At most one overdue notice is sent per loan.
    • Once Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for a loan, the loan is never sent another notice. Notices do not repeat on a schedule.
    • A repeated Send Overdue Notice for a loan whose notice is already recorded succeeds and records nothing, and the gateway hands nothing over for it.
  • INV-OVN-3: Overdue notices go by email only, to the borrower's current email address.
    • Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The address used is the one recorded on Overdue Notice Sent. An email change after that doesn't resend the notice or change where a pending hand-off goes.
  • INV-OVN-4: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded before the notice is handed to the email provider, and every notice handed over has one.
    • The hand-off is driven from the recorded event and repeated with the same key, after a restart too, until the provider accepts it. That is a technical retry, not a failure of the notice.
    • Overdue Notice Sent doesn't mean the borrower received or read the email. Any failure the provider reports later follows this Overdue Notice Sent.
  • INV-OVN-5: No notice is sent for a loan that has ended, because its tool was returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-OVN-6: The notice goes out as soon as the loan is overdue, with no quiet hours.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time. The due date is the latest one set by Tool Checked Out or Loan Extended.
    • A loan that isn't overdue today is refused, for example one extended just before the gateway acted.
  • INV-OVN-7: The notice gives the borrower's name, the tool's name, the due date, a request to return the tool, and that an overdue loan blocks new checkouts and pickups.
  • INV-OVN-9: After Overdue Notice Failed, no further notice is attempted for that loan.
    • The loan already has its Overdue Notice Sent, so INV-OVN-2 already stops a second one. The shed manager follows up in person.
  • INV-OVN-10: The loan must exist.
  • INV-OVN-11: The due date given must be the loan's current due date.
    • The gateway reads it from the list, which may be a moment behind. A notice never states a due date the loan no longer has.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz (ana@example.org) borrowed the cordless drill as loan L1, due 12 October, and hasn't returned it. Today is 13 October in the shed's local time.

  • Happy path (INV-OVN-6, INV-OVN-7)
    • Given: at the start of 13 October, shed time, L1 joined Overdue Loans To Notify
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1, to ana@example.org, for Ana Ruiz, the cordless drill, due 12 October
    • Then: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1 with that address, name, tool name and due date. The gateway then hands the provider an email to ana@example.org, keyed L1, telling Ana Ruiz the cordless drill was due 12 October, asking her to return it, and saying that an overdue loan blocks new checkouts and pickups.
  • Not overdue on the due date itself (INV-OVN-6)
    • Given: today is 12 October
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-overdue: "This loan isn't overdue." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Extended just before the gateway acted (INV-OVN-11)
    • Given: L1 was on the list, and Loan Extended has just moved its due date to 19 October. The list hasn't caught up yet.
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1, giving the due date 12 October
    • Then: refused with due-date-changed: "This loan's due date has changed." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Returned just before the gateway acted (INV-OVN-5)
    • Given: Ana returned the drill, ending L1, and the list hasn't caught up yet
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Recorded lost before the notice (INV-OVN-5)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for L1
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended. No event is recorded.
  • The gateway reads the same loan twice (INV-OVN-2)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1, and the list returned L1 once more before it caught up
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1 again
    • Then: the command succeeds and records nothing new. The gateway hands nothing over, so Ana gets one email.
  • No second notice later (INV-OVN-2)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and the drill is still out a week later
    • When: the gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify
    • Then: L1 isn't on the list, and no further notice is sent.
  • The hand-off call errors (INV-OVN-4)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1, and the gateway's first hand-off call to the provider fails with a connection error
    • When: the gateway repeats the hand-off, keyed L1, and the provider accepts it
    • Then: one email goes to ana@example.org. Nothing more is recorded.
  • The process stops before the provider accepts (INV-OVN-4)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1, and the process stopped before the hand-off was accepted. L1 has already left Overdue Loans To Notify.
    • When: the gateway starts again
    • Then: it hands the notice over from the recorded Overdue Notice Sent, keyed L1, to ana@example.org with the recorded content. One email goes out.
  • A repeat with different content (INV-OVN-2)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1 to ana@example.org
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives giving ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: refused with notice-already-sent: "An overdue notice has already been sent for this loan." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Current email used (INV-OVN-3)
    • Given: Ana changed her email to ana.ruiz@example.net before L1 became overdue
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1 with the list's current address
    • Then: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded with sentTo ana.ruiz@example.net, and the email goes there.
  • Email changed after the notice was recorded (INV-OVN-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1 to ana@example.org, and its hand-off hasn't been accepted yet
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the notice still goes to ana@example.org, the address recorded on it. No second notice is sent.
  • Notice that later fails (INV-OVN-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Overdue Notice Failed was later recorded for it
    • When: the gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify, and a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives anyway
    • Then: L1 isn't on the list. The command succeeds and records nothing new, and nothing is handed over.
  • Unknown loan (INV-OVN-10)
    • Given: no loan L9 has been checked out
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L9 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing, and the gateway hands nothing over for that loan. No person sees these reasons; they are logged with the loan ID. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. loan-not-found (INV-OVN-10).
  2. If Overdue Notice Sent is already recorded for the loan: with the same address, name, tool name and due date, the command succeeds and records nothing; otherwise notice-already-sent (INV-OVN-2).
  3. loan-ended (INV-OVN-5).
  4. due-date-changed (INV-OVN-11).
  5. loan-not-overdue (INV-OVN-6).
Reason Sentence Rule
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-OVN-10
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-OVN-5
notice-already-sent An overdue notice has already been sent for this loan. INV-OVN-2
due-date-changed This loan's due date has changed. INV-OVN-11
loan-not-overdue This loan isn't overdue. INV-OVN-6

loan-not-found, loan-ended and due-date-changed mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan. A missing or malformed loan ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked.

Idempotency: a repeated Send Overdue Notice for a loan that already has its Overdue Notice Sent, with the same content, succeeds and records nothing, and nothing new is handed over. Notices are handed over only from recorded Overdue Notice Sent events.

Hand-off retries: the hand-off is driven from each recorded Overdue Notice Sent until the provider accepts it. A call that errors (the provider unreachable, a timeout), or a stop before acceptance, is repeated with the same key, the loan ID, after a restart too. The provider sends at most one email per key. Delivery attempts after acceptance are the provider's; a final failure is recorded by Record Overdue Notice Failure.

Requests at the same moment: Send Overdue Notice is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan, so at most one Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for a loan.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: Send Overdue Notice is internal. Only the Overdue Notice Gateway issues it; it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • PII & compliance: the email carries the borrower's name, email address and the tool they have. Overdue Notice Sent records the same, as facts of the notice that was sent. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: the notice is recorded within 5 minutes of the start of the day after the due date (the gateway's read interval), and handed over as soon as the provider accepts it.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (this slice): loanId, sentTo, borrowerName, toolName, dueDate.
    • The gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify's items: loanId, dueDate, toolName, borrowerName, borrowerEmail (slices/overdue-loans-to-notify.md).
    • These keys match slices/check-out-tool.md and extend-loan.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Overdue Loans To Notify (the loan leaves it) and My Loans (shows the notice was sent). Record Overdue Notice Failure matches the provider's failure report to the loan by the hand-off key, the loan ID.

Open Questions

None.

g.title: 1. loops back to "Overdue Loans To Notify"
